text:
A: Hi. Hello. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, I can hear you. Hello. How are you?
A: Yeah, not bad, thanks. Bit tired. You?
B: I'm okay, thank you. Little bit tired also. I'm Gurpreet.
A: Nilesh. Nice to meet you.
B: Nice to meet you. Where you are, which area?
A: Kingsbury, North West London. You?
B: Hayes. West side, near Heathrow.
A: Oh right, not too far then. What do you do?
B: I work in food factory, packaging, near the airport. I run the tray-sealing line.
A: No way. Tray-sealing? That's what I do. Park Royal, chilled food. Ready meals mostly.
B: Really? Same machine! Ready meals, sandwiches, yeah, yeah.
A: That's funny. The man I spoke to before, Abdul, he asked me about the little trays with the film on top, and I was trying to explain, and now here's someone who actually knows.
B: Ha. Nobody knows what we do, really. They just buy the lasagne.
A: Exactly. Erm, how long have you been doing it?
B: Er, long time, maybe ten years, different places. Now I'm part-time, three shifts, because my back. I hurt it two years ago, so the physio said, you know, little bit less.
A: Oh, sorry to hear that. Was it at work?
B: Yeah, sort of. Lifting the film rolls, I think, too many times wrong way. It's okay now. Little bit hard sometimes.
A: Yeah, those rolls are heavy. We had a lad do the same last year. I always tell the new starters, get the trolley, don't be a hero, you know.
B: Yeah, yeah, good advice. You train the new people?
A: Yeah, on the sealer, mostly. They keep asking me. I don't mind, really. They're thinking about team leader for me, maybe, but erm, I'm not sure. Half the line are my mates, so telling them off would be, sort of, weird.
B: I did team leader cover one time. Two weeks. Very hard. One guy always late, I have to talk to him, I don't like it. I'm happy to go back to machine.
A: Yeah, that's exactly what worries me. The money would be nice, though. We're trying to save for a deposit, so.
B: Same, me and Simran, my partner. We are saving. London is very expensive, so maybe Slough, something small.
A: Yeah. It feels like it's always just out of reach, you know.
B: Yeah. Slowly, slowly. That's it, really.
A: Do they change your overtime rota a lot? Ours changes every week.
B: Every week! I look on Monday, it's one thing, Wednesday, something else. And people ask me to swap, I always say yes.
A: Ha, me too. I can't say no. My wife says I should, but then I'm stood there and they look at you, and—
